subject: Meteorology
title: Robert FitzRoy
description: A short lesson to help you apply Robert FitzRoy.

hook.text: Robert FitzRoy, captain of the Beagle, became the first person to issue daily weather forecasts to the public.

buildup.text: After a devastating storm sank the Royal Charter in 1859, killing 450, FitzRoy pushed for a storm warning system.

discovery.text: He coined the term 'weather forecast' in 1861—publishing predictions in The Times newspaper.

twist.text: Scientists mocked his forecasts as unscientific—the pressure drove him to depression and eventual suicide in 1865.

climax.text: After his death, the forecasts were cancelled—but public demand forced their reinstatement within months.

punchline.text: He gave us the weather forecast—and paid a terrible price.

quiz.question: What term did Robert FitzRoy coin?
